items.stem: Hybrid delivery is most appropriate when a project:

options.text: Has both a fixed, well-understood part and an uncertain, evolving part
options.rationale: Correct: hybrid suits mixed certainty, applying predictive and adaptive methods where each fits.

options.text: Is fully defined with no uncertainty
options.rationale: A fully defined project favours a predictive approach.

options.text: Has no deadlines or constraints at all
options.rationale: Hybrid is not about the absence of constraints.

options.text: Is too small to need any planning
options.rationale: Size alone does not call for hybrid.

items.explanation: Correct: hybrid suits mixed certainty, applying predictive and adaptive methods where each fits.

items.stem: Which TWO metrics suit a hybrid project's status report? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Schedule and cost variance for the predictive scope
options.rationale: Correct: EVM-style variance tracks the fixed, planned work.

options.text: Velocity or throughput for the adaptive scope
options.rationale: Correct: flow metrics track the iterative work.

options.text: Only the number of meetings held
options.rationale: Meeting count does not indicate progress or value.

items.explanation: Correct: EVM-style variance tracks the fixed, planned work.

items.stem: A common failure when tailoring a hybrid lifecycle is:

options.text: Adding agile ceremonies without changing how decisions are actually made
options.rationale: Correct: ceremonies without behaviour change deliver no benefit.

options.text: Holding a retrospective at the end of a phase
options.rationale: Retrospectives are a legitimate practice to keep.

options.text: Defining milestones for the fixed work
options.rationale: Milestones are appropriate for predictive scope.
A backlog is a sound adaptive practice.

items.explanation: Correct: ceremonies without behaviour change deliver no benefit.
